title: Graver sins cannot stand with a good conscience or title to heaven
source_text: VIII. At vero sunt alia peccata graviora, quae simul stare non possunt cum bona conscientia, & justitia ac sanctitate illa sine qua nemo videbit Dominum, & ad quam omnes qui sunt vere pii & fideles, in hac vita per Christi gratiam renovantur. Unde est quod ipsum gratiae Evangelium illos quibus ordinarium est talia peccata patrare, & qui in aliquo eorum a morte deprehenduntur, absolute pronuntiat regno coelorum excludendos. Ac proinde qui incidunt in ejusmodi peccata, & aliquandiu in iis perseverant, aeternae mortis reatu constricti sunt, & praesentem, ut sic dicam, aptitudinem amittunt ad ingrediendum in regnum coelorum: nec pro tempore illo retinere possunt conscientiae pacem, salutis fiduciam, & gaudium quod est Spiritus Sancti fructus, ac syncerae pietatis & probitatis comes. Neque bene sperare licet de salute ejus quem mors derepente opprimit ejusmodi aliquod grave scelus patrantem. Quale est, verbi causa, adulterium, idololatria, & deliberatum homicidium.
pass_a_gloss: But there are other graver sins which cannot stand together with a good conscience and that righteousness and holiness without which no one will see the Lord, and unto which all who are truly godly and faithful are renewed in this life by Christ’s grace. Whence it is that the Gospel of grace itself absolutely pronounces those for whom it is ordinary to commit such sins, and who are overtaken by death in any of them, to be excluded from the kingdom of heaven. And so those who fall into sins of that kind and persevere in them for some time are bound with the guilt of eternal death, and lose their present fitness, so to speak, for entering the kingdom of heaven: nor for that time can they retain peace of conscience, confidence of salvation, and the joy which is the fruit of the Holy Spirit and companion of sincere piety and uprightness. Nor is it lawful to hope well concerning the salvation of him whom death suddenly oppresses while committing some such grave crime. Of which kind are, for example, adultery, idolatry, and deliberate homicide.
pass_b_english: Grave sins—adultery, idolatry, deliberate murder—cannot share a good conscience or present fitness for heaven.
While they last, peace, assurance, and Spirit-given joy depart; sudden death in them leaves no ground for hope.
